entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice J.Sreenivas Rao
 Writ Petition No.6778 of 2025
Order:

This writ petition is filed seeking the following relief:
" ... to issue a Writ Order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus in not considering the representations of petitioners dated. 01/04/2024,
26/02/2024 and 29/02/2024 and non-initiating to implement the R and R package under Sec 31 of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and GO.Ms.No. 68,
dated.08/04/2025 as being illegal, arbitrary, discriminatory and violative of Articles 14, 19 and 21 of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondents to consider representations of petitioners dated.01/04/2024, 26/02/2024 and 29/02/2024 and act in accordance with Sec 31 of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
GO.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Ms. No. 68, dated 08/04/2025 or any other law/scheme in such locality."

2. Heard Ms.M.Sahithi Sri Kavya, learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition for respondent Nos.1 to 4 and 7 and Sri P.Sri Harsha Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for respondent Nos.5 and 6.
3.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the writ petition is being disposed of at the stage of admission.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that petitioners are illiterates and labourers in Dubbagudem Village, Kasipet, Mancherial District and respondent Nos.2 to 4 acquired their lands for the purpose of Kalyani Khani Open Case Project, in Mandarmri area, Dubbagudem Village,
Kasipet, Mancherial District.
However, respondents have not extended Rehabilitation and Resettlement (R&R) benefits.

At that stage, petitioners have submitted representations before respondent Nos.2 and 3, dated 01.04.2024, 26.02.2024 and 29.02.2024, requesting them to extend Rehabilitation and Resettlement (R&R) benefits under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013) as well as under G.O.Ms.No.68, dated 08.04.2025.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Inspite of the same, respondent Nos.2 and 3 have not taken any steps to consider the same, without any reasons.

5. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition submitted that if the representations submitted by the petitioners dated 01.04.2024, 26.02.2024 and 29.02.2024 are still pending,
respondent Nos.2 and 3 will consider the same in accordance with law and requested this Court to grant reasonable time.

6. Taking into consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and submissions of respective parties and without going into the merits of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to dispose of the Writ Petition, with a direction to respondent Nos.2 and 3 to consider the representations submitted by the petitioners dated 01.04.2024, 26.02.2024 and 29.02.2024 and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, after taking into consideration of the provisions of the Act 30 of 2013 as well as G.O.Ms.No.68, dated 08.04.2025, within a period of eight (8) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, after giving notice and opportunity to the petitioners and respondent Nos.5 and 6.
7.
With the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
